title: Evaluating Large Language Models on Spatial Tasks: A Multi-Task Benchmarking Study

model.params_source: paper Sec. 3.2 (temperature uniformly set to 1 for all models); max_tokens and top_p assumed

task.approximation: automatic scoring for multiple-choice, true/false and objective-answer items (normalized match to the reference = 2, else 0) and an LLM judge on the printed 0/1/2 rubric for subjective and code items replace the human reviewer voting (resolution plan); the partial-credit share will differ

items.source: figshare private share link https://figshare.com/s/be55522f22bf761cfcab (Sec. 10 Data availability): the 900-question spatial benchmark with expert-validated answers

fields.label: reference answer / expected code output
fields.category: task category (12 subspaces, Table 2) and question type (multiple-choice, true/false, objective, subjective)

items.license: unknown (figshare share page; not readable without opening the link)

prompt.system: You are a quiz assistant answering the following questions and outputting the results without any additional explanation.

placeholders.question: items.question verbatim (zero-shot round; no prompt-strategy tuning)

prompt.source_location: Sec. 3.2 (system prompt for the zero-shot round)

output.parse: free text; multiple-choice -> option letter; true/false -> true/false; objective -> normalized string or number; subjective/code -> full reply passed to the judge
output.postprocess: strip, lowercase, remove punctuation for the automatic match; a matched answer scores 2, a mismatch 0; judge returns 0/1/2

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: WA = (2*n2 + 1*n1) / (2*(n0+n1+n2)) x 100, where n_k is the number of answers scored k (Eq. 1)
metric.judge: rule for multiple-choice, true/false and objective items; llm:gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 (to be confirmed) for subjective and code items, prompt = the Sec. 3.3 scoring rubric (2 = fully correct, 1 = partially correct, 0 = incorrect; code: runs perfectly with correct output = 2, minor syntax/logic/format errors = 1, fails or deviates = 0), code items executed where possible
metric.original_location: Table 1, row gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09, column WA (%) (Count S0 260, S1 26, S2 614)

open_points: Choose and fix the LLM judge model for the subjective and code items (the paper used human reviewer voting; gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 is a placeholder a human must approve).

Open the figshare share link and confirm that it holds the 900 questions with reference answers, category and question-type fields (the private-link page is JavaScript-rendered and returns no file list to scripted access)
notes: 2,700 subject calls plus up to 2,700 judge calls per 3 seeds. Table 2 gives per-category WA (e.g. GIS concepts 93.6, simple route planning 8.7) for a cheaper category-level check.
